# Bitizen

> Deterministic pixel avatar people for Node.js and browsers. The same `userId`
> plus the same secret always produce the same figure. Zero runtime
> dependencies, SVG and PNG output, two visual styles.

Install: `npm install @kotuke/bitizen` (Node.js 20+, ESM only).

## Core API

```js
import {
  createAvatarDescriptor,
  generateAvatarPng,
  generateAvatarSvg,
  renderAvatarPng,
  renderAvatarSvg,
  avatarEtag,
  normalizeSize,
  normalizeStyle,
  PALETTE,
  STYLE_NAMES,      // ["plain", "rich"]
  DEFAULT_STYLE,    // "plain"
  AVATAR_VERSION,   // "v1"
} from "@kotuke/bitizen";

// One-shot helpers
const svg = generateAvatarSvg(userId, { secret, style, size, title }); // string
const png = generateAvatarPng(userId, { secret, style, size });        // Buffer

// Reuse one seed for both formats
const descriptor = createAvatarDescriptor(userId, { secret, style });
renderAvatarSvg(descriptor, { size, title });
renderAvatarPng(descriptor, { size });
```

Options:

- `secret` — required string, at least 16 characters. Keep it on the backend.
- `style` — `"plain"` or `"rich"`, default `"plain"`. Unknown value throws `RangeError`.
- `size` — integer 32…2048, default 256. Out of range throws `RangeError`.
- `title` — SVG accessible title, escaped automatically.

Errors: empty `userId` or non-string throws `TypeError`; short secret, bad size
or unknown style throw `RangeError`. Nothing is ever written before validation.

## Browser entry point

```js
import { generateAvatarSvg } from "@kotuke/bitizen/browser";
```

Same figures byte for byte, seeded by a bundled SHA-256 instead of `node:crypto`.
SVG only — PNG needs zlib and stays Node-side.

## HTTP server

```js
import { createAvatarServer } from "@kotuke/bitizen/server";
const server = createAvatarServer({ secret, maxCacheEntries: 512 });
```

Routes: `GET /avatars/v1/<urlencoded-id>.(svg|png)?size=512&style=rich` and
`GET /health`. Responses carry `ETag`, `Cache-Control: immutable` and CORS
headers; unknown style returns 400, unknown version 404.

## Descriptor shape

```js
// style "plain"
{ version, fingerprint, accent, pixels: [[column, row], …], eyes, rows, style }

// style "rich"
{ version, fingerprint, accent, scheme, layers: [{ color, pixels }], eyes, rows, columns, style }
```

`fingerprint` is the first 16 bytes of the HMAC as lowercase hex — safe to store
and log; the raw `userId` never appears in the output.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- Determinism key: `AVATAR_VERSION + AVATAR_SECRET + style + userId`. Changing
  any of them changes the picture; changing the secret rotates every avatar.
- Both styles render on a flat black field; the figure is one connected shape of
  square modules, and eyes are always white.
- `plain` figures are always mirrored, `rich` figures are asymmetric about half
  the time and can carry a second colour plus body cutouts.
- Visual collisions are possible in principle: 0 repeats per 100,000 users for
  `rich`, 26 for `plain` on the reference secret.
- Throughput on the build machine: SVG ≈ 0.2–0.3 ms, PNG ≈ 0.8–1.0 ms per avatar
  at 256×256.
